title: Nephi records upon plates of ore
summary: Nephi makes plates of ore and engraves records upon them. He distinguishes these from the first plates, which contain his father's record and genealogy and most of their wilderness proceedings.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord commanded Nephi to make plates of ore to engrave the record of his people.
Nephi engraved his father's record, their journeyings in the wilderness, his father's prophecies, and many of his own prophecies upon the plates he made.
At the time he made these plates, Nephi did not know he would be commanded by the Lord to make them.

Nephi says the first plates contain his father's record, his father's genealogy, and most of their proceedings in the wilderness; things that transpired before he made these plates are more particularly recorded on the first plates.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi making plates of ore and engraving them.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance, tools, surroundings, and the plates' precise design.

narration.text: “wherefore I did make plates of ore”
“that I might engraven upon them the record of my people.”

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses distinguish the plates Nephi made here from the first plates.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord appearing; no appearance is described.
Do not invent a specific location or workshop.

title: The plates’ purpose
summary: Nephi recounts a commandment about what should be written on these plates and their purpose. He describes a record on other plates about his people’s wars, contentions, and destructions, and instructions for what should happen after he is gone. He says an account of making these plates will be given hereafter.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi received a commandment that the more plain and precious parts of the ministry and prophecies should be written on these plates, and that these writings should be kept for his people’s instruction and other wise purposes known to the Lord.
Nephi made a record upon the other plates, which gives a greater account of his people’s wars, contentions, and destructions.

Nephi commanded his people what they should do after he was gone, and said the plates should be handed down from one generation to another, or from one prophet to another, until further commandments of the Lord.
Nephi says an account of his making these plates shall be given hereafter, and that he proceeds as he has spoken so the more sacred things may be kept for his people’s knowledge.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown writing or speaking about the plates, without depicting the reported commandment as a present event.
unspecified_visual_details: The plates’ appearance, Nephi’s appearance and clothing, the setting, and whether anyone else is present.

narration.text: “this I do that the more sacred things may be kept for the knowledge of my people.”

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The commandment and account are reported retrospectively; no divine appearance is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord appearing or add dialogue from him.
Do not stage wars, destructions, or the plates being handed down as current events.

title: What Nephi writes
summary: Nephi says he writes upon plates only what he considers sacred, acknowledges his weakness, and describes how some people set at naught what others value, including God and the voice of his counsels.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says he writes nothing upon plates unless he considers it sacred and acknowledges his weakness according to the flesh.
Nephi says some people set at naught what others esteem valuable, including God, and do not hearken to the voice of his counsels.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown with plates while writing or reflecting.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance, expression, posture, and setting.
The appearance of the plates and writing implement.

narration.text: Nevertheless, I do not write anything upon plates save it be that I think it be sacred.
And now, if I do err, even did they err of old;
For the things which some men esteem to be of great worth, both to the body and soul, others set at naught and trample under their feet.
Yea, even the very God of Israel do men trample under their feet;
I say, trample under their feet but I would speak in other words—they set him at naught, and hearken not to the voice of his counsels.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The trampling language is figurative; do not depict people physically trampling God.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God as a visible figure; no appearance is described.
Do not literalize the figurative trampling.

title: A prophecy of his coming and suffering
summary: Nephi declares that he cometh six hundred years from the time his father left Jerusalem. He prophesies that the world will judge him to be a thing of naught, and that he will be scourged, smitten, and spat upon, which he will suffer.

explicit_facts.text: He cometh six hundred years from the time Nephi’s father left Jerusalem.
The world will judge him to be a thing of naught; they will scourge and smite him, and he will suffer it.
They will spit upon him, and he will suffer it because of his loving kindness and long-suffering towards the children of men.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be depicted as the source of the prophecy, without depicting the future events as occurring in the present.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi’s appearance, posture, and activity; the location; the identity and appearance of the one prophesied of; the people who will mistreat him.

narration.text: “And behold he cometh, according to the words of the angel, in six hundred years from the time my father left Jerusalem.”
“And the world, because of their iniquity, shall judge him to be a thing of naught;”

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses present a prophecy; the future mistreatment is not described as occurring in Nephi’s present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the future scourging, smiting, or spitting as present events.
Do not invent an appearance for the one prophesied of or identify the people who mistreat him.

title: Prophecy of crucifixion and darkness
summary: The verse says the God of the fathers yields himself as a man into the hands of wicked men, to be lifted up, crucified, and buried in a sepulchre. It says three days of darkness should be a sign of his death to inhabitants of the isles of the sea, especially those of the house of Israel.

explicit_facts.text: The God of the fathers, also called the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, yields himself as a man into the hands of wicked men, to be lifted up, crucified, and buried in a sepulchre, according to the words of the angel, Zenock, Neum, and Zenos.
Three days of darkness should be a sign of his death to those inhabiting the isles of the sea, especially those of the house of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The verse may be presented as written or spoken prophecy without depicting the prophesied events as happening.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance, identity, and setting of any person presenting the prophecy are unspecified.
The appearance of the God of the fathers and the wicked men, and the settings of the prophesied events, are unspecified.

“to be lifted up, according to the words of Zenock, and to be crucified”

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports what is to happen and cites earlier prophetic words; it does not narrate these events as happening in the present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the crucifixion, burial, or three days of darkness as present events.

title: Prophecy of signs and upheaval
summary: The prophet describes the Lord God visiting the house of Israel in different ways. Zenos says the signs and the rending of the rocks must come, and that many kings of the isles of the sea will be moved by the Spirit of God to exclaim that the God of nature suffers.
characters: Kings of the isles of the sea (mentioned)

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God will visit all the house of Israel; some hear his voice because of their righteousness, unto joy and salvation, while others experience signs of his power.
The signs named include thunderings, lightning, tempest, fire, smoke, vapor of darkness, the opening of the earth, and mountains carried up.
Zenos says all these things must come and that the rocks of the earth must rend.
Because of the groanings of the earth, many kings of the isles of the sea will be wrought upon by the Spirit of God to exclaim, “The God of nature suffers.”

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the passage as prophecy rather than portraying its predicted events as occurring in the narrator’s present.
unspecified_visual_details: The prophet's identity in verse 11, the Lord's appearance, the identities and appearances of the kings, and specific locations are not given.

“The God of nature suffers:”

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses state these events as prophecy; they do not describe them as occurring in the narrator's present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the predicted signs as occurring in the narrator's present.
Do not invent the Lord's visible appearance or identify the prophet in verse 11.

title: Prophecy concerning Jerusalem
summary: The prophet says those at Jerusalem will be scourged by all people because they crucify the God of Israel and turn their hearts aside, rejecting signs and wonders and God's power and glory. They will wander in the flesh, perish, become a hiss and a byword, and be hated among all nations.

explicit_facts.text: The prophet says those at Jerusalem will be scourged by all people because they crucify the God of Israel and turn their hearts aside, rejecting signs and wonders and the power and glory of the God of Israel.
The prophet says they will wander in the flesh, perish, become a hiss and a byword, and be hated among all nations because they turn their hearts aside and despise the Holy One of Israel.

title: Promises to the House of Israel
summary: The prophecy says that when they no more turn aside their hearts against the Holy One of Israel, he will remember the covenants made to their fathers, remember the isles of the sea, and gather in the house of Israel from the four quarters of the earth. All the earth shall see the Lord’s salvation, and every nation, kindred, tongue, and people shall be blessed.

explicit_facts.text: When they no more turn aside their hearts against the Holy One of Israel, he will remember the covenants he made to their fathers.

All the earth shall see the salvation of the Lord, and every nation, kindred, tongue, and people shall be blessed.

title: Nephi's purpose and burden
summary: Nephi says he wrote these things to persuade his people to remember the Lord their Redeemer. He speaks to all the house of Israel if they obtain these things, describes spiritual workings that weary him and weaken his joints for those at Jerusalem, and says the Lord showed him concerning them. He says the Lord showed prophets of old things concerning them and showed many concerning his people; these things are written on the plates of brass.
